title: Battery Light On
summary: Charging-system workflow for battery warning lights, low voltage, belt slip, and alternator estimate continuity.
intro: A battery light usually means the vehicle is not charging correctly, but the estimate should still separate battery condition, alternator output, belt drive, fuses, cables, and grounds.
common_sounds: Dimming lights or weak blower speed
Belt squeal near startup or with load
Vehicle may stall after battery reserve is depleted
quick_checks: Load test the battery before judging alternator output
Measure charging voltage with electrical loads on
Inspect serpentine belt, tensioner, and pulley alignment
Check alternator output cable, main fuse, and engine grounds
Scan for low-voltage codes and module resets
inspection_priority: Belt and cable voltage-drop checks before alternator replacement
confidence_cues: Belt slip can mimic alternator failure
Low voltage can create many secondary codes
common_causes: High resistance in charge cable, fuse, or ground

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Alternator Output Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Use when a known-good battery still shows low charging voltage.
checks: Measure voltage at battery and alternator output
Check main charging fuse or fusible link

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Belt and Battery Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Use when belt slip or weak battery condition may be creating the warning.
checks: Inspect belt cracking, glazing, and tensioner travel
Check for parasitic drain if battery repeatedly dies

recommended_repairs.title: Alternator Blueprint
recommended_repairs.description: Use after charging voltage, belt, and cable checks support alternator failure.

recommended_repairs.title: Serpentine Belt Inspection
recommended_repairs.description: Use when squeal, glazing, or tensioner movement suggests belt slip.

recommended_repairs.title: Battery Test
recommended_repairs.description: Use before final charging-system approval when battery state is unknown.
